result.reason: The clause reaches the fallback and most of the preferred position: it adds a mutual greater-of cap, retains a mutual indirect/consequential-damages exclusion, includes indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP-infringement carve-outs, and excludes Sparkling’s payment obligations from damages. Confidentiality appears to be covered through Sections 13 or 14, although data protection and security are not expressly identified, so full preferred compliance cannot be confirmed. The final sentence is unnecessarily broad: stating that all limitations in Section 15 do not apply to Excluded Claims may disapply the direct-damages limitation and consequential-damages exclusion, rather than merely making those claims uncapped. It should instead state that only the aggregate cap does not apply, subject to the existing treatment of Sections 13 and 14. The cap also uses the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to the claim rather than the 12 months preceding the claim.
